upsertSlices.task: Distributed proper edge coloring in synchronous rounds
assumptions: Simple graph, n vertices, maximum degree Δ.
Synchronous LOCAL model; unrestricted message size and local computation.
Distinct identifiers as in the standard LOCAL model.
Main view fixes Δ ≥ 3 independently of n.

yAxis.label: Communication rounds at fixed Δ ≥ 3 (symbolic order)

results.bound: O(log¹²Δ + log n) or Õ(log^(5/3)n) LOCAL rounds
results.notes: Two alternative instantiations. The constant-degree main view specializes the first. O(log n) is tight here only after fixing Δ. A bound on reduction overhead alone is not a bound on the whole algorithm.

results.bound: Ω(log_Δ n) deterministic; Ω(log_Δ log n) randomized LOCAL rounds
results.notes: Even on 2-vertex-colored trees. Randomized lower bound uses the high-probability RandLOCAL correctness requirement. The 2026 erratum changes a network-decomposition claim; it explicitly leaves the edge-coloring bounds unchanged.

results.bound: O(log¹²Δ + log log n) or Õ((log log n)^(5/3)) LOCAL rounds
results.notes: Total randomized runtime includes the residual (2Δ−1)-edge-coloring subroutine. Fixing Δ reduces the first instantiation to O(log log n).

upsertSlices.label: LOCAL; deterministic near-Δ palette
upsertSlices.task: Compute a proper edge coloring in synchronous LOCAL rounds
assumptions: Simple graph, n vertices, maximum degree Δ.
Synchronous LOCAL model; unrestricted message size and local computation.
Distinct identifiers as in the standard LOCAL model.
ε > 0 is fixed.
Exactly (1+ε)Δ colors requires Δ ≥ c√log n for sufficiently large c.

yAxis.label: Algorithm model (categorical); inspect exact round formulas

results.bound: O(log²n) + Õ(log²Δ · log n) LOCAL rounds
results.guarantee: Proper edge coloring with q = (1+ε)Δ + O(√log n)
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 3 and the following additive-term discussion
results.notes: The all-degree statement contains an additive palette term. It cannot be plotted as a fixed near-Δ palette in the bounded-degree main view. When Δ = 2^{O(√log n)}, runtime is O(log²n). This is the LOCAL theorem, not the slower CONGEST theorem. Full proof is the accepted DISC 2026 preprint, distinct from the published PODC brief announcement.
